intent: To illustrate the timing and severity of the sharp surge in daily confirmed coronavirus cases in India beginning in early 2021.

units.meaning: The line represents India's daily confirmed COVID-19 cases, specifically a 7-day moving average ('daily cases 7dma').
accepted_routes: India's daily COVID-19 cases, 7-day moving average
The curve tracks India's daily cases, smoothed over 7 days
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must have a label/title or legend identifying the entity as India daily cases 7dma.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly name both the metric (daily cases/7dma) and country (India)?

units.meaning: The sharp surge begins late in the series, after a low near 15.8 around x_px 972-977, not at the beginning of the plotted period.
accepted_routes: The surge starts after a late low near 16
Cases first fall to about 15.8 before climbing steeply in the final part of the chart
The steep increase begins in the final segment, not at the series start
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show a trough/low before the final steep upward segment; the surge should not be read as the initial rise.
units.reviewer_question: Is the late-series timing/onset, not just any increase, required?

units.meaning: By the final plotted point, the 7-day average reaches about 369.5 daily cases.
accepted_routes: The plotted series ends at roughly 370 daily cases
units.visual_evidence_rule: The final endpoint/value should be visible or labeled on the y-axis or annotation.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'sharp increase in coronavirus cases' clause
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show the final endpoint value, or is showing the steep rise enough?

units.meaning: From the pre-surge low to the final point, cases increase by about 353.7 (from ~15.8 to ~369.5), a roughly 23.4-fold rise.
accepted_routes: Cases rose about 23-fold from the late low
From about 16 to about 370, an increase of roughly 354 cases
The final level is roughly 23 times the pre-surge low
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both the pre-surge low and final high must be visible, or the rise must be quantified in an annotation.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video quantify the fold-change/difference from the late low to the endpoint?

units.meaning: The final surge crosses the 100, 200, and 300 case thresholds in quick succession.

basis.note: first value above 100 in final surge
first value above 200 in final surge
first value above 300 in final surge

accepted_routes: Cases pass 100, then 200, then 300 during the surge
The 7-day average crosses 100 near x_px 1097, 200 near x_px 1120, and 300 near x_px 1136
It breaks through 100/200/300 thresholds as it accelerates
units.visual_evidence_rule: Horizontal reference lines or annotations at 100, 200, and 300 should be shown with the curve crossing them.
units.reviewer_question: Are threshold crossings required, or are they optional visual evidence of steepness?

optional_valid: The series had an earlier local peak near 97.8 at x_px 628.9 before declining to the late low.
The final relative_value is 0.9133, but it should not be interpreted as a share/proportion without axis metadata.
The series is plotted as a 7-day moving average, which smooths daily volatility.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims about variants, lockdowns, festivals, elections, or other drivers.
Extrapolating beyond x_px=1150 or claiming the final value is the maximum in the full pandemic if the table only ends here.
Using relative_value as a percentage/share of population or cases.
Stating exact dates beyond the narration without an x-to-date mapping in the table.
notes: The table has only x_px and values, so date labels should be sourced from the narration/axis, not inferred. U5 is a deliberate optional threshold unit to make the severity trade-off visible.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
